a novel approach of transcriptional gene silencing in E. histolytica.
the development of a gene-silenced strain of E. histolytica with a significantly attenuated virulence.
the silencing of genes of interest in E. histolytica and the use of this phenomenon for vaccine development.

the silencing of genes of interest is feasible in trophozoites of strain HM-1.

the silencing of the Ehap-a gene in trophozoites of E. histolytica strain G3 was due to a truncated SINE1 element in the 5′ upstream regulatory region of the gene and that this element was able to silence other genes in trophozoite cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the silencing of two genes is possible in trophozoites of E. histolytica strain G3 and that this silencing is stable in the absence of the silencing plasmid.
the silencing of multiple genes can be achieved in a single step by using SINE1 sequences.
silencing of multiple genes in E. histolytica trophozoites is possible and that it can be accomplished by a single plasmid.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is now possible to silence genes in trophozoites of E. histolytica, and this silencing is not limited to a specific region or gene.
the silencing of multiple genes in the same cell may be possible by a single transfection with a construct containing the upstream region of a gene and a truncated SINE1 sequence.
the transcriptional silencings of two genes in E. histolytica trophozoites is possible and that the silencing of other genes may also be achieved.
